text:
maria.dev: Heads up — saw a couple of failed decrypts when trying to restore a staging snapshot just now. Error is `AccessDeniedException: permission denied for cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`

alex.sre: omg, where did this happen? staging or prod?

maria.dev: staging, snapshot id `stg-snap-20260321-09`. Happened at 2026-03-21T09:12Z. I pulled the object metadata and the `cmek` header is missing for that object. :eyes:

paul-sec: I rolled the RBAC prune last night at ~02:00Z, removing a few long-unused uploader service accounts. Could be related. Which principal was trying to decrypt?

maria.dev: the restore job runs as `backup-uploader@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (legacy). The job log shows it tried to call KMS decrypt but got the AccessDenied.

clair-encops: Do we have KMS audit entries for the decrypt call? If the grant was pruned we should see a `DENY` in Cloud Audit Logs for `google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt`

maria.dev: I looked — there's a hole in the audit logs between 01:58Z and 02:05Z for the KMS key in question. No `SetIamPolicy` entries either. Strange.

sre-bot: Incident detected: 3 failed decrypts for `projects/redwood-ops/locations/global/keyRings/backups/cryptoKeys/snap-key` between 2026-03-21T09:12Z and 09:13Z. Pager runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/encops-snapshot-restore>

alex.sre: Could be a timing window where RBAC prune + KMS key rotation overlapped and some grants were garbage-collected. Do we use ephemeral grants or grant tokens for the uploader job?

clair-encops: Our system supports both. Most backlog restores use ephemeral grants with a TTL of 24h, but legacy jobs rely on static IAM binding. If the service account was removed from IAM on the key, static binding would fail immediately.

paul-sec: I confirmed I removed `backup-uploader@...` from the key-binding in the prune. It was on a “unused principals” list. I did not touch vault grants. Sorry, my bad — missed the legacy job.

maria.dev: no worries. Can we quickly re-grant for staging so restores succeed? Also need to figure out why the audit logs have a gap.

paul-sec: Re-adding now. Command:```bash
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding snap-key \
  --location global --keyring backups \
  --member serviceAccount:backup-uploader@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```

paul-sec: done — I just re-added the binding and pushed an updated IAM policy. :thumbsup:

maria.dev: Retry restore — starting now.

maria.dev: Restore succeeded. Thanks. :relieved:

alex.sre: We still need to investigate the audit log gap. Could be export ingestion delay or a logging agent restart around 02:00Z. Who owns the logging pipeline?

clair-encops: I'll check logs for the Stackdriver ingestion agent and the GCP audit-export sink. Also check if the KMS key had a rotation event around that time — rotation can briefly change cryptoKeyVersion states and generate extra IAM events.

maria.dev: For postmortem: recommend we run an automated canary restore in staging immediately after any RBAC prune or IAM change that touches keys/roles. Also whitelist any legacy service accounts until migration.

paul-sec: Agreed. Action items: 1) Paul to add temporary policy and run audit-scan to list all principals with active restores (ETA 2hrs). 2) Clair to check logging pipeline and provide reason for audit gap (ETA 4hrs). 3) Maria to add canary restore step to RBAC-prune playbook and file a migration ticket for backup-uploader (ETA EOD).

alex.sre: I created a high-level ticket: TICK-4582 to track followups (includes playbook edit + retrospective).

clair-encops: Quick remediation note that might help if this recurs: for ephemeral/short-lived workflows, prefer using KMS `testIamPermissions` before a restore to fail fast and emit an alert. Example: `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions snap-key --permissions=cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`

maria.dev: adding that to the canary checklist. Also capturing the failed log snippets here for the postmortem:```text
2026-03-21T09:12:17Z restore-runner: Decrypt call failed: AccessDeniedException: permission denied for cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt
2026-03-21T09:12:18Z restore-runner: aborting restore, snapshot stg-snap-20260321-09
```

paul-sec: We'll update the RBAC-prune checklist to run a quick inventory `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` across keys used by backups and assert no referenced principals are removed.

alex.sre: 👍 Looks like immediate impact contained to staging. We should decide if we need a company-wide notification or just update the RBAC playbook.

paul-sec: I'll prepare a short blurb for ops-updates and tag affected owners.

maria.dev: thanks all. Filing the postmortem draft now. :memo:

sre-bot: Postmortem draft created: <https://redwood.internal/postmortems/pm-2026-03-kms-prune-staging>

clair-encops: Follow-up checklist in ticket TICK-4582: add canary, add `testIamPermissions`, ensure audit-export monitoring alerts (new alert threshold for missing audit entries >1m).

maria.dev: sounds good. closing thread for now, will ping when draft is up. :wave:
